about.titleLine1: From making things with my hands
about.bio: I'm Naïm, a product designer and AI builder based in Tunisia. I enjoy taking ambiguous ideas, giving them structure, designing the experience, and turning them into something people can actually use.
about.heroHeadline: I DESIGN. I BUILD. I EXPERIMENT.
about.heroLead: I turn complex problems into usable digital products through product design, AI, low-code, and automation.
about.journeySubtitle: A visual progression connecting physical engineering, visual craft, human-centered UX, low-code delivery, and autonomous AI systems.

1.title: Mechanical Design & Fabrication
1.exp: Learning how physical things are designed, manufactured, and refined under real-world constraints; developing a rigorous, practical approach to problem-solving.
1.lesson: Physical constraints teach you that every millimeter matters before production begins.

2.title: Graphic & Visual Design
2.exp: Turning concepts into visual communication and developing a sharp intuition for typography, layout hierarchy, contrast, and visual clarity.
2.lesson: Clarity is kindness; design begins with how information is perceived and understood.

3.title: UX/UI & Product Design
3.exp: Understanding human mental models, mapping user journeys, and structuring cohesive, accessible digital experiences across web and mobile platforms.
3.lesson: The best interface is the one that removes friction between the human and their goal.

4.title: Low-Code & Implementation
4.exp: Connecting design decisions directly to production application behavior, data structures, and APIs—bridging the gap between design vision and engineered reality.
4.lesson: A design is only as strong as what actually ships and survives production.

5.title: AI Product Building & Automation
5.exp: Experimenting with agentic workflows, Model Context Protocol (MCP), API automations, and LLM orchestration to build connected, intelligent digital systems.
5.lesson: AI expands the leverage of one builder, but human discernment defines the taste and quality.

about.philosophyIntro: Tools evolve every month, but how you approach problems remains your true craft. Here is how I think before touching any tool.

1.title: Understand before designing
1.body: Deconstruct the real problem and its operational context before deciding what to build. Avoid rushing to solutions before framing the root necessity.

2.title: Design with implementation in mind
2.body: A design should account for real technical constraints, performance bottlenecks, and state transitions so that usability is preserved in production.

3.title: Experiment to learn
3.body: Test assumptions through rapid functional prototypes, measure real behavior, and iterate relentlessly rather than assuming the first idea is optimal.
